idiom_name: position-keyed container (uniform grid, hash grid, quadtree, R-tree) kept in sync with movement
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: pick a partition unit (uniform grid for evenly spread movers, hash grid for unbounded worlds, quadtree/octree for clustered or hierarchical spaces, R-tree for rectangle-shaped queries) and an index function that maps position or bounds to the unit. Keep three operations behind one interface - insert, remove and query(region) - and make every code path that changes a position or destroys an object call remove plus insert (or mark dirty and rebuild once per tick). Queries enumerate only the cells overlapped by the region, deduplicate members that span several cells, and run the exact predicate afterwards; the structure stays a filter, never the authoritative object store.
code_sketch:
partition = make_partition(world_bounds, cell_size)
partition.insert(obj)                  # at spawn
partition.move(obj)                    # remove + reinsert on position change
partition.remove(obj)                  # at despawn
candidates = partition.query(region)   # visits only overlapping cells
results = [o for o in candidates if exact_predicate(o)]
pitfalls: Skipping the membership update on one movement path leaves stale entries that return wrong neighbours silently.
Storing the authoritative object state inside the partition makes the structure the object store and blocks swapping it.
One cell size copied without measurement: either almost everything lands in one cell or almost every cell is empty.

Wrong move: answer a radius query by reading only the cell containing the query point -> failure: every member whose nearest point lies in an adjacent cell is silently missed whenever the radius exceeds roughly one cell -> instead: visit every cell the query region overlaps (ceil(radius / cell_size) cells in each direction), or size cells so the typical radius fits the visited block.

Wrong move: insert or remove members from inside a query's per-cell iteration (spawning or killing entities while handling overlaps) -> failure: the container mutates under the iterator, skipping or double-visiting members mid-query -> instead: collect membership changes in a queue and apply them after the query phase, or snapshot candidate ids before acting on them.

Wrong move: index an object only in the cell containing its position when its bounds span several cells -> failure: region queries that touch only the object's other cells never see it and the candidate set is wrong -> instead: register the object in every cell its bounds overlap (and deduplicate on query) or route oversized members to a hierarchical structure.
